narrative: Material PL1__M863E17A exhibits smooth, stationary Normal demand (mean 119,264 units/day, CV 0.334) with no detectable trend over the observation period. Lead times are variable (mean 1.85 days, CV 0.704), with lead time variability contributing 89.2% of total lead-time-demand variance. The recommended (r,Q) policy sets safety stock at 270,833 units and order quantity at 431,836 units (EOQ-driven, well above MOQ), reducing total annual costs by 85.4% while maintaining 95% service level and staying well within storage capacity.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, stationary Normal demand with fully characterised lead times makes the (r,Q) model the analytically optimal choice. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs without simulation, and the Normal safety stock formula is valid given near-zero skewness.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Peak inventory (702,669 units) represents 53.4% of storage capacity (1,315,337 units), leaving 612,668 units of headroom. No capacity constraint binds; the recommended policy is fully feasible.
